sections.title: Habit and leaves
sections.text: Downy oak is a medium-sized deciduous tree of southern and central Europe and western Asia. It commonly reaches about 15–20 m, with a broad, irregular crown. Its lobed leaves are grey-hairy beneath, and young shoots are softly hairy.

sections.title: Acorns
sections.text: The acorns mature in one year, often in clusters of three or four; they are roughly 1–3.5 cm long and partly enclosed by a hairy-scaled cup. The sources consulted describe acorns as wildlife food but do not establish safe human preparation or species-specific toxicity.

sections.title: Comparison
sections.text: It differs from evergreen Quercus ilex and from North American Q. rubra by its deciduous leaves and downy leaf undersides. Q. rubra instead has sharply pointed lobes.
